title: Folarin Balogun shown straight red card in USA’s World Cup round-of-32 game against Bosnia
author: Paul Tenorio
content:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. — Folarin Balogun was shown a straight red card in the 64th minute of the U.S. men’s national team round-of-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina after a video review of a foul on Tarik Muharemovic.

As the ball was played up the left sideline from Antonee Robinson in the 61st minute, with the U.S. leading 1-0, Balogun reached out and tried to get his body in position. As he did so, he landed on the back of the leg of Muharemovic, raking down the calf and landing on the defender’s ankle.

It did not look like an intentional foul, but rather the forward landing awkwardly. On the slow-motion replay, however, it looked like a strong tackle. And there was no doubt that Balogun made rough contact on the defender.

After being instructed by the Video Assistant Referee to go to the pitchside monitor to review the incident, on-pitch referee Raphael Claus told Levi’s Stadium that Balogun had committed a “serious foul” and would be sent off.

Balogun was stunned by the decision, and was consoled by Christian Pulisic and a Bosnia player. He stood still for about 15-20 seconds on the field before slowly walking toward the tunnel. Several U.S. subs, including Tim Weah, went up to comfort him as he neared the corner flag.

Balogun, 24, scored the opening goal for the U.S. and had arguably been the best player on the field for the Americans through the first hour of the game.

Whereas the U.S. wasted chances four years ago, Balogun has been a consistent danger man in this World Cup. That continued into the knockout stage. The Monaco striker had a goal called back for offside in the 31st minute, but then gave the U.S. a 1-0 lead in the 45th minute with a neat left-footed finish.

Balogun broke out LeBron James’ “Silencer” celebration, which earned a tweet from the NBA legend.

The U.S. heavily recruited Balogun coming out of the Qatar tournament, with fans aiding in that chase with their all-out press on social media. Balogun has proven to be worth it, producing across his national team career.

The New York-born, London-raised striker now has three goals in this World Cup, tied for second-most for U.S. men’s player with Landon Donovan (2010) in a single tournament. Bert Patenaude (1930) holds the USMNT record with four.

Balogun watched the remainder of the knockout game from the sideline — including Malik Tillman’s free kick to make it 2-0 that sealed the win — and will automatically miss the round of 16 game against Belgium.

FIFA, which organizes the World Cup, has the power to extend Balogun’s ban if its disciplinary committee chooses to meaning he could miss further games should the U.S. progress further in the tournament.

Analysis by senior football writer Stu James

The red card felt harsh and Balogun’s reaction to the referee’s announcement — the U.S. striker looked absolutely stunned and didn’t leave the pitch immediately — said it all.

The Video Assistant Referee team can intervene if they feel a “clear and obvious error” has been made by the on-field referee, or there was a “serious missed incident.”

In this case, the VAR recommended that the referee review Balogun’s challenge on Muharemovic. Rarely in that scenario will a referee look at the pitch-side monitor and stick with his on-field decision, although they are free to do so.

There’s no suggestion that Balogun’s challenge on Muharemovic was deliberate. It was accidental and a clumsy coming-together more than anything. But when an incident is shown in slow motion — and that was the case here — the contact always looks so much worse.

There’s an argument that replays should be shown in real time, to give a fairer perspective, but that’s never been the case with VAR.

By George Edwards

Claus was appointed by FIFA to officiate only his second match at this World Cup, having taken charge of Spain’s 4-0 victory over Saudi Arabia in the second round of group matches.

The 46-year-old gave out two yellow cards in that game, and was instructed by the VAR to rule out a fifth Spain ‘goal’ in stoppage time for offside, blowing the full-time whistle moments later.

Claus officiates in the Brazilian domestic league, and is one of 12 referees at the tournament from Conmebol, the South American football confederation.

This is Claus’ second World Cup after featuring at the Qatar edition in 2022, where he took charge of two group matches: England 6-2 Iran and Canada 1-2 Morocco.

He has been on FIFA’s list of referees since 2015, and took charge of the 2024 Copa America final in Miami, where Lautaro Martinez’s extra-time winner saw Argentina beat Colombia 1-0.

Claus has handed out one red card in 23 international matches and he averages 4.4 yellow cards per game in the Brazilian Serie A in 262 matches.
